title: Prices Recovered. Foreign Selling Persisted.
deck: The recovery broadened, but conviction remains limited. IHSG rose 0.94% as foreign selling eased. All five large caps in our focus still recorded estimated foreign net selling in the regular market.

blocks.text: IHSG ended the week at 6,093.759, up 0.94%. Participation improved: 548 stocks advanced and all eleven sector indices finished higher. Foreign investors remained net sellers across all stock markets, although the Rp2.45tn weekly sale was smaller than the previous week. The index gave back part of its early gain after Tuesday, then recovered some ground on Friday.

blocks.label: Assessment
blocks.text: Our view is cautiously constructive on breadth, with limited confirmation from foreign flows. Friday's small official net purchase was encouraging, but the regular-market estimate remained negative. We keep the company discussion focused on five liquid large caps with a documented earnings base.

Tuesday's intraday high was 6,216.439. Thursday closed at its session low of 6,031.284, below the previous Friday's close. On Friday, the index traded as low as 5,995.821 before recovering. These ranges describe the week's volatility. They have not been tested as support or resistance.

sections.title: An early advance meets a midweek test

blocks.caption: The session ledger: all stock markets

blocks.text: BBCA, BBRI and BMRI contributed to Monday's advance. The index rose again on Tuesday despite a decline in BBCA, before turning lower on Wednesday.

Thursday was the weakest session: 518 stocks fell, with BBRI, AMMN, BMRI and BREN among the largest negative contributors. BBRI, AMMN, TLKM and BBCA helped Friday's rebound. These contributions show how prices moved the index; they do not establish what drove investors' decisions.

Healthcare and transport held up on Thursday, gaining 0.70% and 0.61% while the other nine sector indices declined. Both rose again on Friday. Their weekly outperformance therefore included resilience during the sell-off.

Official foreign net selling fell 51.4% to Rp2,445.80bn from Rp5,036.31bn in the previous week. The improvement matters, but it was mostly a reduction in selling: foreigners sold on each of the first four days. Friday's Rp30.40bn net purchase offset only a small part of those sales. At the close, IDX's year-to-date total remained a net sale of Rp84,999.31bn.

blocks.label: THE FOREIGN-FLOW PULSE
blocks.title: A small Friday purchase followed four days of selling
blocks.note: IDX official foreign trading values across regular, cash and negotiated stock markets.

blocks.text: The regular-market estimate showed Rp141.60bn of foreign net selling on Friday. The five companies in our focus also recorded a combined estimated net sale that day. This can coexist with the positive official all-market total because the coverage and valuation differ. Regular-market estimates value foreign share volumes at each day's close; official trading values reflect execution prices.

blocks.caption: Two views of foreign demand: Rp bn

blocks.text: Stock trading value totalled Rp81.129tn. Average daily value rose 28.52% to Rp16.226tn, while average daily share volume fell 7.62% and trading frequency declined 0.27%. Higher turnover therefore came without an increase in shares traded or trade counts on those weekly averages.

Wednesday dominated the turnover story. Of Rp36.193tn traded, Rp27.478tn was in the negotiated market, about 75.9% of the day's value. BYAN accounted for Rp26.186tn, or 72.35% of total stock value. The concentration is clear; the reports do not disclose counterparties or transaction purpose. BYAN is relevant to the turnover analysis and is outside our company focus.
Regular-market value averaged Rp9.793tn a day. On Friday it fell to Rp8.576tn from Thursday's Rp11.306tn, even as the index rebounded. The price recovery thus came with lower regular-market turnover.

sections.title: A wider recovery, an uneven path

blocks.text: The weekly breadth breakdown shows 548 stocks advancing, 222 declining and 193 unchanged out of 963. The corresponding shares are 56.9%, 23.1% and 20.0%. We calculate these from the published counts: the percentages printed beside the two declining groups appear to be transposed.

blocks.label: THE PARTICIPATION MAP
blocks.title: All eleven sectors finished higher
blocks.note: Official IDX sector-index price returns. These cover each index, not the five-stock company focus or a selected-stock basket.

blocks.text: Transport and logistics led with a 5.85% gain, followed by healthcare at 3.59% and basic materials at 2.10%. Financials rose 0.31% and industrials 0.14%. The recovery was broad over the full week, but Thursday's sharp decline shows how uneven the path remained.

We focus on BBCA, BBRI, BMRI, TLKM and ASII. All five exceed Rp100tn in market value and Rp50bn in average daily regular-market trading over the latest 20 sessions, with no zero-volume session in that window. Each has disclosed positive reported first-half earnings. This is a selected group for closer analysis, rather than every company passing the size and liquidity screen.

Four of the five shares rose despite estimated foreign net selling in the regular market: ASII gained 4.10%, TLKM 3.11%, BBRI 0.65% and BMRI 0.25%. BBCA fell 0.82%. Their price performance was stronger than the foreign-flow reading. The data do not identify the ultimate buyers or explain their motivation.

blocks.caption: The earnings base: six months to 30 June 2026

blocks.text: For the banks, earnings provide a starting point. Asset quality and funding determine how durable those earnings are. BBCA reported June NPL of 1.9% and loans at risk of 4.9%. BMRI's June snapshot showed NPL of 1.01% and capital adequacy of 17.9%. Margins, funding costs and credit quality remain the key follow-up checks.
BBRI's publication separates profit attributable to the parent from total group profit. Credit costs and micro-loan performance warrant attention at the next earnings review.
Telkom's opening results summary reported Rp34.9tn of operating cash flow alongside Rp10.6tn of reported profit. The next review should test cash conversion and capital spending.

Astra's reported profit declined 19% to Rp12.533tn, while net debt excluding financial-services subsidiaries reached Rp6.0tn. Mining and equipment earnings deserve particular attention. Positive profit alone does not resolve these risks.

These disclosures cover the period to June and were released before this trading week. They establish an earnings base and identify financial risks; they do not explain October price moves or establish fair value. We assign no new company rating or target price.

blocks.label: THE INDEX DRIVERS
blocks.title: How four focus companies contributed to IHSG
blocks.note: ASII, TLKM, BBRI and BBCA appear in IDX's weekly top-ten contributor lists. BMRI does not appear there, so no exact weekly contribution is inferred for it.

blocks.text: In IDX's weekly ASEAN comparison, Indonesia's 0.94% gain trailed the Philippines at 1.28% and exceeded Thailand at 0.38%. Vietnam, Malaysia and Singapore declined. Collection times differ, so the comparison should not be read as a set of simultaneous exchange closes.
Friday's JISDOR was 17,884 rupiah per dollar, compared with 17,898 in the prior audited edition. The dollar reference rate fell 0.08% between those Fridays.

Within the current workbook, the move from Monday's 17,917 to Friday's 17,884 was a decline of 0.18%. These are different windows: the supplied workbook covers 5 to 9 October, and the earlier Friday is sourced separately.

blocks.label: The next test
blocks.text: The next test is whether the broader recovery gains consistent flow and trading support. We would look for repeated positive official daily foreign flows, an improvement in regular-market estimates, participation across profitable large caps, and turnover less dependent on negotiated transactions. The current week provides partial evidence, rather than confirmation.

For BBCA, BBRI and BMRI, track earnings, asset quality, credit costs and funding alongside price and flow. For TLKM, focus on reported profit and cash conversion. For ASII, assess whether mining and equipment earnings recover. These are the next research questions, not forecasts for next week's prices.

Our assessment rests on the supplied market observations and dated issuer disclosures. We leave unsourced explanations open and treat the week's highs and lows as observed ranges, rather than trading signals.

method: Price returns exclude dividends and costs. Rp bn means billions of rupiah; Rp tn means trillions. IDX official foreign values cover all stock markets. The rounded daily foreign figures sum to -Rp2,445.79bn; the weekly report prints -Rp2,445.80bn, a Rp0.01bn rounding difference. Regular-market foreign estimates cover the regular market and use foreign share volumes times each day's close; the displayed official-minus-estimate gap is not an attribution of negotiated foreign flow. Aggregated regular-market value and share volume match all five supplied daily RG lines exactly. Market cap uses shares outstanding times close. ADTV uses the 20 regular-market sessions ending 9 October and was independently recalculated. The five-company focus is editorial and has documented positive first-half earnings, not a valuation assessment or a comprehensive investment-quality screen. Rounded financial metrics retain their issuer definition. Breadth follows the chart colors and legend; percentages are recalculated from counts. JISDOR and equity closes are set at different times, so dollar returns are indicative and exclude fees, taxes and hedging. The 2 October JISDOR baseline comes from the prior audited edition.
